title: The agentic economy

title: Virtual agent economies

sentence: Existing research on LLM biases has focused primarily on content-based effects such as anchoring on numerical values (Lou & Sun, 2024) and serial position effects in list evaluation (Guo & Vosoughi, 2024).
title: Anchoring bias in large language models: an experimental study

sentence: Existing research on LLM biases has focused primarily on content-based effects such as anchoring on numerical values (Lou & Sun, 2024) and serial position effects in list evaluation (Guo & Vosoughi, 2024).
title: Serial position effects of large language models

sentence: Research on anchoring bias demonstrates that LLMs are disproportionately influenced by initial information presented in prompts, with stronger models showing greater susceptibility to anchor hints (Lou & Sun, 2024).
title: Anchoring bias in large language models: an experimental study

sentence: Valencia-Clavijo (2025) provide both behavioral and attributional evidence that anchors shift entire output distributions in LLMs, with effects varying by model scale.
title: Anchors in the machine: Behavioral and attributional evidence of anchoring bias in llms

sentence: Serial position effects, including primacy and recency biases, have been confirmed across various tasks and models, though their intensity varies and prompt-based mitigations show inconsistent effectiveness (Guo & Vosoughi, 2024).
title: Serial position effects of large language models

sentence: Yin et al. (2025) uncover strong order effects in LLM-driven comparisons, including a novel centrality bias and quality-dependent shifts between primacy and recency preferences.
title: Fragile preferences: A deep dive into order effects in large language models

sentence: Echterhoff et al. (2024) introduce a comprehensive framework for evaluating cognitive biases in high-stakes decision-making, demonstrating that prompt-induced, sequential, and inherent biases persist across commercial and open-source models.
title: Cognitive bias in decision-making with llms

sentence: Rothschild et al. (2025) articulate the vision of an “agentic economy” where assistant and service agents interact programmatically to facilitate transactions, arguing that the architecture of agentic communication will determine whether generative AI democratizes economic opportunity.
title: The agentic economy

sentence: Bansal et al. (2025) develop Magentic Marketplace, a simulated two-sided marketplace where assistant agents represent consumers and service agents represent competing businesses, revealing that all models exhibit severe first-proposal bias creating  $ 10-30\times $ advantages for response speed over quality.
title: MAGENTIC MARKETPLACE: AN OPEN-SOURCE ENVIRONMENT FOR STUDYING AGENTIC MARKETS

sentence: Tomasev et al. (2025) propose frameworks for analyzing emergent AI agent economies, discussing auction mechanisms for fair resource allocation and the socio-technical infrastructure needed for trust and accountability.
title: Virtual agent economies

sentence: Research on LLM negotiation and strategic behavior includes NegotiationArena (Bianchi et al., 2024), which evaluates LLM negotiation abilities across ultimatum games, trading games, and price negotiations, finding that agents can boost outcomes through behavioral tactics.
title: How well can llms negotiate? negotiationarena platform and analysis

sentence: Guo et al. (2024) propose competitive games as dynamic evaluation environments, demonstrating that LLMs exhibit varying levels of rationality and strategic reasoning.
title: Economics arena for large language models

sentence: Shapira et al. (2024) introduce GLEE, a unified benchmark for language-based economic environments that enables systematic comparison of LLM behavior to human players.
title: Glee: A unified framework and benchmark for language-based economic environments

sentence: Park et al. (2023) demonstrate that generative agents can simulate believable human behavior in interactive sandbox environments, establishing foundational architectures for multi-agent simulations.
title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

sentence: Zheng et al. (2020) introduce the AI Economist, using two-level deep reinforcement learning to discover tax policies that trade off equality and productivity, demonstrating that AI-driven policies can outperform traditional economic frameworks.
title: The ai economist: Improving equality and productivity with ai-driven tax policies

sentence: Byrd et al. (2019) develop ABIDES, an agent-based market simulation environment that enables research on trading algorithms and market dynamics.
title: ABIDES: TOWARDS HIGH-FIDELITY MARKET SIMULATION FOR AI RESEARCH

sentence: Chen et al. (2023) introduce AucArena for evaluating LLM strategic planning in auction settings, finding that while LLMs demonstrate skills for effective bidding, even advanced models are occasionally surpassed by heuristic baselines.
title: Put your money where your mouth is: Evaluating strategic planning and execution of llm agents in an auction arena

sentence: We evaluate EBR using the Magentic Marketplace (Bansal et al., 2025), an open-source two-sided agentic marketplace environment that simulates a complete transaction lifecycle including search, messaging, proposal submission, and payment.
title: MAGENTIC MARKETPLACE: AN OPEN-SOURCE ENVIRONMENT FOR STUDYING AGENTIC MARKETS
